#1882. Palmeiras vs Estudiantes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

After 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

In the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

Palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

Abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

Although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

In Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

Estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

Their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

Palmeiras’ medical staff are racing to get defender Murilo fit after he sustained a left-thigh injury. If he is unavailable, Bruno Fuchs is expected to join captain Gustavo Gomez and Alexander Barboza in the back three, ahead of youngster Luis Benedetti.

Forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

Fellow full-back Jefte remains provisionally suspended pending a hearing before the Anti-Doping Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-AD).

For Estudiantes, former Sao Paulo midfielder Gabriel Neves is still recovering from a fractured arm and is likely to miss out.

Neves joins midfielder Baltasar Rodriguez, who is suspended after being sent off in the second leg of the semi-final.

Joaquin Correa sustained a grade-two muscle injury to his right thigh against Talleres on November 7.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.

Miguel; Gomez, Murilo, Barboza; Giay, Freitas, Pereira, Piquerez; Arias, Roque, Lopez

Muslera; Mancuso, Nunez, Palacios, Rojo; Piovi, Burgos, Castro, Palacios, Cetre; Carrillo

With two solid, well-organised defences and goalkeepers in good form, a high-scoring contest seems unlikely.

Palmeiras may dominate possession, but Estudiantes could respond with a set-piece goal if they fall behind.

If the final goes to penalties, Muslera could have the chance to redeem himself after a difficult World Cup.

Ruben Amorim became the AC Milan head coach in the summer, but he was far from the only name the management considered.

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s new manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

“In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” said the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

“You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he said.

“If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

#1875. Donyell Malen, 2026’s top scorer, on the radar of Europe’s biggest clubs?

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 12:02

Donyell Malen has been a new man since arriving at Roma. With the Dutch striker the top league scorer in Europe's big five leagues in 2026, can he join one of Europe's best clubs?

Struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan. The Dutch striker has stepped up a level since moving to the Italian capital, and he is enjoying an exceptional 2026 calendar year with 26 league goals.

That makes him the top scorer across Europe's five biggest leagues over that period, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe (21 goals). His current success has not gone unnoticed and led Roma to invest £21.3m (€25m) to sign the best recruit of 2026 permanently.

Malen has not been affected by the permanent transfer and is continuing on excellent foundations at the start of the season. He now has 12 goals in 11 Serie A matches, and must also add five goals and two assists in five Champions League matches.

The versatile forward, who was often used on the flanks at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, has been installed as the number nine by Gian Piero Gasperini with great success.

The Dutchman's performances are logically starting to attract more prestigious suitors.

With Kane injured at Bayern Munich and Doue and Kvaratskhelia injured at PSG, Malen's name has been cited as a target for both giants.

The two-time European champions are looking for a versatile forward for January, which is exactly what Malen is. His profile fits Paris's needs.

However, PSG do not want to overpay, and as things stand Roma have no interest in selling their star man, who is under contract until June 2030, in the middle of the season unless an exceptional offer arrives. A transfer in January therefore looks very unlikely, even to Bayern Munich, where he would also make a lot of sense with Kane absent for several months.

On the other hand, if Malen continues in this vein, the approaches should multiply next summer. A move to one of Europe's heavyweights could also appeal to the Roma forward, with the Italian club potentially struggling to keep hold of him and to turn down huge offers.

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that said, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

#1869. Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

Granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the new manager.

Aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

But what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'

It was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

It was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

His previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message quickly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

This is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

He has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

The contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

The attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

Frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

That may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

None of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

But there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

#1866. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Possession: Ipswich 41%-59% LiverpoolShots: 8-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 7-12

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Palacios, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.Substitutes: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, McAteer, Clarke, Flemming.

"Everyone's going to love him" 😍Jamie Redknapp is looking forward to seeing Bradley Barcola play for Liverpool this evening! pic.twitter.com/Ut9Zx4gbB2

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

"He is the talisman already inside these first two games"Can Julio Enciso provide another assist tonight? 👀 pic.twitter.com/FaDkndt3BG

"I'm desperate for him to do well!" Jamie Redknapp says Florian Wirtz has to produce more for Liverpool right now 💭 pic.twitter.com/1fYT9t9tx3

A milestone appearance for Dom 🫰🔴 pic.twitter.com/C28iemsxou

"I really feel they've got that recruitment right' Luke Chambers says the Premier League experience of players that Ipswich have signed will be massive for them 🧠 pic.twitter.com/DgwYsTlHBD

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1865. Fabian Hürzeler gives brilliant answer to Gary Lineker's Brighton title race theory

Gary Lineker argued that the Seagulls could become genuine title contenders – and be ‘very difficult to stop’ – if they had a striker in the mould of former Leicester City forward Jamie Vardy.

All-time leading Premier League goalscorer Alan Shearer agreed but also praised the quality of recent performances, including the surprise defeat at Hull City.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Hürzeler insists he is happy with the attacking options already at his disposal, pointing to Brighton’s goalscoring record and the number of players capable of finding the net. Albion lead the Premier League goals scored table, finding the net 26 times in 11 games.

Asked about Lineker and Shearer’s praise for Brighton as one of the most entertaining teams in the league, Hürzeler welcomed the recognition but stressed that performances, rather than outside opinion, must remain the priority.

“If they say this, of course we should listen to it,” he said.

“On the other side, being the best football team doesn't mean you automatically win games.

“We really have to keep focusing on our performances, that’s what we can control. We can't control what others think about us.

“We can only control how well we prepare for a game and how high our levels are on matchday.

“The truth is always on the pitch, and therefore we have to get back to our highest level.”

Hürzeler was more emphatic when asked whether he agreed with Lineker’s suggestion that Brighton were missing a clinical, traditional centre-forward.

“An Alan Shearer?” the German replied, tongue-in-cheek.

“No, no. I think we have a lot of good strikers. When you look at how many goals we've scored in the season so far, and how many goals we scored today.

"We might not have one striker but we have plenty of players who are able to score goals.

“That's what has made us strong in the past and what will make us strong in the future, hopefully on Sunday as well.”

The Brighton head coach was speaking after his side responded to their disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City with a 4-0 victory over Craiova in the UEFA Conference League.

Next up is a home match against Newcastle United, in the Premier League, this weekend.

Hürzeler specifically named the attacking players he believes can provide the goals, making clear that he has no concerns about the options available to him.

He added: “We're very happy with Kostoulas. We're very happy with [Georginio] Rutter.

"We're also happy with Tobi [Promise David], who came onto the pitch today against Craiova.”

The head coach also appeared keen to ensure that the defeat at Hull did not define the assessment of his team's attacking play.

Brighton created opportunities at the MKM Stadium but were unable to find a way past an inspired goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis, prompting Lineker to suggest that a striker with Vardy's instincts could make them much harder to stop.

Hürzeler, however, would rather focus on the wider picture than one frustrating afternoon in front of goal.

“We're focusing on the positives,” he said.

"We are not focusing on one game where we missed a few chances.”

The 4-0 victory over Craiova offered an immediate reminder of Brighton's goalscoring capabilities, although Hürzeler will now want his players to carry that performance into Sunday's match.

#1864. Romano: Cardinale remains ‘key player’ in Milan’s transfer business despite Krösche’s arrival

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Markus Krösche will soon get to work at AC Milan, but Gerry Cardinale will remain involved.

It has not been a very well-kept secret that Milan have been pushing for the arrival of Krösche since the summer, when it looked as though the German director was all set to arrive alongside Ruben Amorim, before Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rather than turn to an alternative appointment, the Rossoneri decided to internally promote some figures while leaving the vacancy open. Ultimately they were waiting for developments on Krösche, and he officially left the Bundesliga side last month, leaving him available to finally join.

On Monday, there was talk of a release clause paid to Eintracht. In a video published on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano revealed some added information about Krösche’s imminent arrival and what it will mean regarding Cardinale’s involvement.

“Confirmation has arrived, and I would say finally, also from Germany of something we have been telling you for weeks: Markus Krosche will be the new Head of Football at Milan. In Germany there has been a much slower narrative, much more, let’s say, Eintracht-centric,” he said (via MilanNews).

“The reality is that Milan has had an agreement with Krosche for some time, Milan also has everything ready for the official announcement which is expected shortly. Milan will not pay 5 million, but 4 million euros in compensation to Eintracht Frankfurt to free Krosche, who already said goodbye to the German club some time ago.

“He will be ready and operational from the beginning of December to work on the winter transfer market with Gerry Cardinale, Ruben Amorim and the entire work group that is dealing with Milan. So there were never any doubts whatsoever.

“Markus Krosche is ready to take control of the Rossoneri mercato with Gerry Cardinale, who will be absolutely present, a key player, and involved. After Milan’s excellent victory against Frosinone, the Milan owner reiterated that if Milan competes for a player, it will be to win, not to participate. In short, this is another sign of Milan’s ambition.”

#1863. Peterborough United vs Cambridge United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:12

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an important victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Peterborough United form (all competitions):

Cambridge United form (all competitions):

Peterborough could welcome back Ben Woods and Luca Mendonca on Saturday, but they are both unlikely to start even if they are fit.

Savage is expected to keep faith with the team that beat Plymouth last weekend, with Leonard set to lead the line with support out wide from Bolu Shofowoke and Owura Edwards.

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:

Peterborough should have renewed confidence after their victory over Plymouth and we are expecting a tight, hard-fought derby clash.

The Japan international is recovering from a hamstring injury which required surgery and has kept him out since May.

#1858. Man United's January transfer budget will be less than £50m with Mauricio Pochettino expected to make only TWO signings - despite needing to bolster their attack and defence

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

It’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s new financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

United also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January

Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre)

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

McGeehan admits that listening to opposing managers and pundits continuing to label Barnsley as a good footballing side is becoming 'boring'.

#1854. GdS: Strong bonds, Ramos and signings – five reasons for Milan to believe in the Scudetto

AC Milan are five points behind the somewhat surprise league-leaders Lazio, but belief is growing regarding a Scudetto push.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan re-emerged from the two-week international break and put in arguably their best performance of the season against Frosinone. They scored five goals and it could have been more, racking up a third league win in a row to move back into the top four.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The table remains quite tight at the top, with Inter the only team to slip up over the weekend, and the Rossoneri are firmly in the running. The paper highlights give reasons that a title fight is very possible.

Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim are inextricably linked, and that might seem obvious, given that one is the owner and the other the coach. In reality, the bond is deeper than usual, for one simple reason.

Amorim has been handed the keys to create the ‘new Milan’, one that Cardinale has decided to manage completely differently since the end of May. The Portuguese is the coach to whom RedBird have given the longest contract so far, and Cardinale believes he’s the right man at the right time.

He’s demonstrating this concretely not only with his constant presence and his reassuring words, but also with his intention to improve the squad quickly and with the arrival of a key management figure like Markus Krösche. Now, Amorim will receive even greater support.

Gonçalo Inacio, Nicolo Tresoldi, Endrick. These are just some of the names circulating – and these aren’t rumours, but actual targets – ahead of a potentially crucial January transfer window.

The question is obvious: with a couple of top-notch signings for the second half of the season, how far could this team go? Staying up there for starters remains the minimum objective, with Champions League football a must.

Then, Amorim and co. hope that the rest will follow, if their rivals begin to lose pace. The coach is starting to make his team look like they are clicking, but Cardinale has realised the need to accelerate to fill the remaining gaps in the squad.

Amorim (fortunately) quickly realised that the average tactical level of his colleagues in Italy is too high to allow himself to present his Milan team in the same way every single way. So, the 3-4-2-1 that was previously seemingly set in stone has become plasticine in his hands.

The manager moulds and shapes the playing system based on the opponents, rather than his own needs. Since Ruben the fundamentalist became Ruben the quick-change artist, we’ve seen a bit of everything: 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3, 4-4-1-1, 3-5-2.

The former Sporting CP coach coach locks himself in the lab throughout the week and tailors the formation he deems best. Sometimes he gets it wrong, but most of the time he gets it right.

Milan have won five of their last six league games and, game by game, they are increasingly able to camouflage themselves effectively tactically. Opponents never know what formation they will face, while Amorim has several players capable of playing well in multiple roles, which helps.

The data is remarkable and reads as follows: only Rocco (29) and Czeizler (31) coached Milan sides that have scored more goals than Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 Serie A games in charge.

In short, despite all the problems involved (Goncalo Ramos in particular, more on him to come) the coach’s attacking vocation is clearly visible. Furthermore, it is a Milan with a high conversion rate in proportion to the shots on target.

It is also a Diavolo side that have somehow found a way to make up for Ramos’ poor contribution in terms of goals. Alphadjo Cisse, Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot take turns to set each other up and score, a sign of a growing offensive physiognomy.

More often than not, a striker simply needs to get a goal in order to build confidence and then begin a virtuous cycle. Milan hope that this is the case for Ramos, who ended his month-long goal drought on Sunday.

However, the reflection goes further: while the Rossoneri having the luxury of being able to score without goals from their No.9 (who is currently on three in the league), surely things can only get better from here?

In short, if the Portuguese international actually does start firing more regularly, then Milan might unlock another dimension to their attack that could really see them surge towards that elusive Scudetto.

#1852. Silly Leeds United punishment shows Daniel Farke's serious approach to complacency

Earlier in the season, the German manager told The Yorkshire Post of his – slightly tongue in cheek – horror at Ao Tanaka wearing gloves in training before the weather had turned cold, and this week he gave a member of staff a dressing down to try and keep his squad grounded after Saturday's hugely impressive 4-1 win at Chelsea.

Both the "crime" and the punishment were light-hearted but with a serious message about complacency, and it is a balance Farke always looks to strike.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Leeds are in seventh in the Premier League and have consistently been around the likely positions to qualify for Europe this season, but Farke has always taken a two-pronged attitude towards expectations, encouraging supporters to get ahead of themselves but not those who work for him.

"What I can guarantee is I will make sure that no one here at the training ground at Thorp Arch is too big time and I'm not one per cent concerned about my players," he said when the topic of Europe was raised ahead of Saturday's Premier League visit from newly-promoted Coventry City.

"We had a staff member this week who came out after a great win against Chelsea more or less celebrating in the first session.

"I know it's a bit colder right now and you have to put yourself into warm clothes but instead of wearing a hat (for training) – a hat is totally fine – he was wearing a snood over his head like a 20-year-old creative No 10 who enjoys himself.

"It was as if he had won the game at Chelsea all alone.

"It was a long working day for him, I made sure. He was treating our kit men and from now on he stays in shorts and T-shirts until the end of January on the outside pitches.

"I don't allow anyone to be big time, not one staff member, not one player. We know exactly what we're coming from and if anyone thinks we are too good for this and can be cool like a 20-year-old No 10, one of my staff members, I will make sure that everyone is back to work and doesn't enjoy himself too much.

"We have not achieved 38 points so far (his mark for avoiding relegation), so there's no reason to lean back, just enjoy and stop working.

"It's good to be already on 17 points at this stage (11 games in). It's definitely a good amount and gives us confidence and belief in what you're doing.

"But at this level the momentum can change quickly and for that we won't allow ourselves to be too big time or to enjoy ourselves too much.

"We are in a good mood at the moment and we work, train and play with confidence but nothing else.

"The Premier League is the best league in the world. We can only win points if we are 100 per cent on it."

A silly response to a seemingly trivial offence (with a much more serious underlying issue) is a balance Farke is conscious of striking.

"It's perhaps not typical for a German fella to have a good sense of humour – at least that's a bit the reputation – but I think in general everyone is at his best in every job when you feel valued, when you feel comfortable when you do your job with confidence and this is also what we try to create," commented Farke.

"I've seen some statistics that we were the hardest-working side over the last (Premier League) weekend. At Chelsea we covered more distance and high-speed intensity runs than any other team at Premier League level.

"This is one side of how we work really hard with focused, concentrated work but we always want to do this with a smile on our face.

"We want to make sure that everyone enjoys coming to work and it's not just hoping for the next day off so I don't see the manager, the staff member or assistant coach.

"Sometimes you have to give them a day off but we also want to create an atmosphere where everyone feels safe and is allowed to make a joke and also joke at my costs.

"You also give the sign that you know how important and how serious football is but it's never more important than the human being.

"When I name the squad on Friday there are some tough decisions and top players won't make it. When I name the starting line-up it's tough for them but then we have to make sure that we have something to cheer and to laugh about.

"Hopefully the most important thing is success and winning points but also to have a good atmosphere.

"I hope my jokes are not too old-school for the players because I'm getting older and older."

Meanwhile, striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract until the end of 2028-29, by when he will have just turned 32.

"I want to keep my best players without giving them the scenario that they can lean back because they've signed a ten-year deal," said his manager. "I've made it clear (to the board) but it was easy because everyone in our hierarchy wants to keep the best players."

#1849. Doncaster Rovers 2 Huddersfield Town 3: 10-man Terriers emphatically end their barren league streak at bogey venue

Certainly for the victor, if there happens to be one.

Do the business, put your feet up - well, sort of - with three points in the bag ahead of a long weekend and watch the rest of your divisional rivals sweat it out.

That was the hope for both Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their differing third-tier missions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The incentive for Rovers was moving out of the drop zone up to 18th, while Town’s ambition revolved around securing the win that would draw them level with leaders Stockport County at the right end of the table.

Huddersfield were the ones smiling as they finally made hay at league level at what had previously been a bogey ground.

The first ever visitors here back on New Year’s Day 2007 - the 20th anniversary is in a month’s time - Town had not so much as scored in any of their previous four visits at league level.

They emphatically put paid to that on a night when they played with a man light for around an hour. You didn’t really guess.

For the first 34 minutes, this game simply wasn’t a contest. There were 19 places between these two rivals ahead of kick-off and it showed as Town cruised into a 2-0 lead, courtesy of Cameron Humphreys’ first goal of the campaign and a 15th strike of a goal-laden season for Joe Taylor before Bali Mumba’s Donny demons resurfaced.

In the league fixture here in February, a panicking handball saw him concede a penalty in the game-breaking moment.

In the present, he was the guilty party again - towards the same goal. He hauled down Jamie Sterry, who got on the wrong side of him following Robbie Gotts’ spotter’s badge of a pass.

Booked earlier for a sliding challenge he couldn’t complain about, Mumba was dismissed for a second yellow card—his second dismissal of the season.

Isaac Hutchinson sent the underemployed Matt Young the wrong way to make it 2-1 and out of nowhere, we had a game on.

But Town, not Rovers, grabbed the all-important fourth goal.

Unconvincing at the back, the hosts erred for a third time and Ilias Bronkhurst fired in a soothing third.

Even without an extra player, it was Town who had the wit going forward as Rovers lacked penetration and quality. Given their defensive charity, it wasn’t a good mix and it's easy to see why they are where they are in the standings.

A stoppage-time goal from home captain Owen Bailey revived Rovers, but it was not enough. Nowhere near.

Rovers, without the ineligible Alfie May under the terms of his loan, handed a first start to loanee James Collins, now finally over his long-term knee injury.

It was a psychologically important night for the veteran striker, who was injured almost exactly a year to the day on December 2, 2025 - ironically against Town. It was his last start.

Collins, who turns 36 on Tuesday, was afforded an early birthday present in the process. Sterry also returned to the Rovers’ starting line-up following illness. Brandon Hanlan dropped to the bench, with Tom Nixon absent.

Joe Low and Fletcher - lined up from the off for Town, coming in for Ibane Bowat and Bojan Radulovic.

Ahead of the game, Martin Drury had spoken about Rovers’ set-piece threat, with Low’s promotion seemingly something to do with that.

A gulf in class saw Town stroll most of the first-half, aided by the meek defensive tendencies which Rovers had avoided five days earlier at Bradford City. It eventually changed.

The promotion of Ashley Fletcher, who had delivered a fine cameo in the Trophy game here in early autumn - looked the shrewdest of moves from Drury.

He teed up Humphreys for an easy low finish for Town’s opener on five minutes after Mumba’s cross caused initial consternation as Rovers prevaricated at the back terribly.

Town mixed play up impressively and afforded themselves plenty of control and possession.

Last-ditch defending from ex-Terriers man Matty Pearson blocked Bronkhorst’s goalbound effort. A similarly alert block from Jack Senior repeated the trick to deny Low.

Town’s second was not long in coming on 21 minutes with Rovers again spooked by Fletcher, who showed adept chest control and neat footballing skills to set up Taylor, who fired home a clinical low volley as Rovers again stood and watched.

A brief half-chant of 'We turn up, why don't you' arrived from disgruntled Rovers patrons in the Black Bank.

Mumba’s indiscretion changed the complexion of the night and Thomas spurned a chance to level before the break, planting a free header over.

Ahead of the resumption, Grant McCann threw on another attack-minded player in Hakeeb Adelakun. His side saw a lot of the ball in the opening part of the second period, but couldn’t conjure a big chance against 10-man Town.

It was the visitors, who still possessed the killer instinct.

Sanches Fernandes rattled the crossbar and from the resultant corner, Rovers’ defensive deficiencies again re-surfaced.

The ball found Bronkhorst and after his initial effort was blocked, he rammed home a low drive in front of the ecstatic 1,905 Terriers supporters.

Bailey ensured there was a nervy finale for the visitors, firing home from Adelakun's low cross. But it was Town's night, deservedly.

Doncaster Rovers: Simkin; Sterry, Grehan (Ayinde 70), Pearson, Senior, Thomas (Husband 84); Gotts, Bailey, Broadbent (Adelakun HT), Hutchinson (O’Reilly 65); J Collins (Hanlan 65). Substitutes unused: Clarke, Bryne. Huddersfield Town: Young; Balker, Low, Roughan; Bronkhorst, A Collins (Ledson 69), Humphreys, Mumba, Sanches Fernandes (Bowat 84), Taylor (Radulovic 84); Fletcher (Harness 55). Substitutes unused: Alnwick, Gooch, Ashia.

Attendance: 8,376 (1,905 Huddersfield Town supporters).

#1847. The Women's World Cup is coming home... but 2035 cannot be treated as a fix for the game's problems, writes TARA ANSON-WALSH

Published: 14:36 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:04 EST, 23 November 2026

The United Kingdom will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, the first football World Cup to be staged on these shores since 1966, it was announced to much fanfare on Monday.

Yet while the countdown can now officially begin, the biggest challenges facing the women's game cannot be kicked eight-and-a-half years down the road.

Over in Zurich, FIFA president Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup, describing a time when they 'didn't exist'.

'We all remember the last Women's World Cup,' the embattled 56-year-old Italian said, calling it 'a huge success'.

The irony, of course, is that the last Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand is remembered by many for all the wrong reasons, with newspaper back pages peppered with images of Spain captain Jenni Hermoso's kiss with the former president of Spain's FA, Luis Rubiales, for days after the final.

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England in Sydney.

Gianni Infantino undertook his usual long-winded and self-serving monologue which precedes these ceremonies, in which he heralded the 'incredible growth' of the Women's World Cup

Rubiales was later convicted of sexual assault for the incident, which triggered widespread protests across the country and overshadowed Spain's terrific 1-0 triumph over England

There is an added layer of irony in that Infantino had, two days before the 2023 final, angered many women worldwide with yet another controversial speech in which he told them: 'You have the power to change', but that they had to 'convince us men what we have to do'.

Alongside this patronising statement, Infantino also insisted that equal pay at the World Cup 'would not solve anything'.

Three years later, Infantino is unfortunately still at the helm, while UEFA's attempts to unseat him following his controversial bid to sell off the World Cup now look to have failed spectacularly, with the football despot increasingly likely to secure a fourth term.

What the social and political landscape will look like by the time this women's footballing bonanza arrives on these shores in 2035 remains unclear. What is clear, however, is that the game's continued progress will require more than the record attendances and soaring commercial revenues the FA are predicting.

It will require the figures who have too often held it back to finally step aside, and that process should begin with the likes of Infantino being shown the door.

It will require those at the top of English football to put their heads together and work out how to stem falling attendances in the league. The average attendance across the first eight WSL matchweeks of 2024-25 was 8,173. Last season it was 7,472. This season, it is tracking at around 5,677.

And third, it will require somewhere other than Wembley to stage the final.

Wembley was, of course, the scene of Chloe Kelly's moment of madness, yet by the time the 2035 Women's World Cup comes around it will also have hosted the men's finals of Euro 2024 and 2028.

The FA paid off its debt on the national stadium in 2024, 17 years after its reopening, and is no longer obligated to host major events there to service repayments.

The rules have been left open for another venue to emerge to host the final, such as Man United's proposed new 100,000 stadium

While under current FIFA regulations, Wembley is the only one of the proposed 22 stadiums that meets the requirements to host a final, the rules have been left open enough for another venue to emerge should a suitable stadium be completed before 2035.

Step up Sir Jim Ratcliffe, although please refer back to point one in this regard – the Manchester United co-owner who famously asked former captain Katie Zelem 'what do you do here?' while touring the club's women's facilities.

United's proposed new 100,000-seater stadium was included in the 2035 bid and could yet come under consideration from FIFA.

While there are still many hurdles to clear before then, hosting a tournament final in Manchester would undoubtedly be huge for the women's game, not least given the optics of a bid built around being 'all together', described as 'a rallying cry to unite people through football'.

London should not be the epicentre of the tournament, not if the intention is to spread the women's game across the United Kingdom rather than concentrate it in the capital, where Arsenal's attendances continue to dwarf those of every other WSL club.

In other words, the women's game in this country cannot be put on hold until 2035.

It cannot afford to wait eight-and-a-half years for this World Cup to come and rescue it. Time to get cracking.

#1846. Huddersfield Town boss on 'well-connected' win at Doncaster Rovers, Bali Mumba red and injury update on Archie Collins

Town, who needed to win to go level on points at the top with League One leaders Stockport County, eased to a 2-0 lead inside 21 minutes, thanks to strikes from Cameron Humphrys - his first of the campaign - and top-scorer Joe Taylor.

But Bali Mumba's second dismissal of the season - a second yellow card for hauling down Jamie Sterry on 34 minutes - gave Rovers hope with Isaac Hutchinson scoring from the resultant penalty.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But despite being a man light, the visitors produced an organised and controlled second half and managed to add a killer third just before the hour mark, courtesy of Ilias Bronkhorst.

Home captain Owen Bailey pulled one back in stoppage-time, but Town held out for a deserved triumph, their first ever in the league at this venue and following up their win in the Trophy at the Club Doncaster Sports Village at the start of September.

Drury said: “I thought we started the game really well and I really liked the way that the players showed real courage and belief early doors with the ball.

"I felt we competed really well in duels in moments where we had to be good because of the energy that Doncaster have and to score two goals early on, I felt we were in real control of the game at that point.

"These things happen in football, so we have to respond from that. We're down to 10 men and it's about not just managing the game, but managing certain moments within the game.

"I thought the players were excellent, I thought they were outstanding.

"We had to defend some big moments towards the end of the game. We tried to get the subs right in terms of not just personnel, but actually size of people coming on in context to what the game might throw at us.

"Obviously, later on, you're expecting more set plays, more crosses into the box from the opponent, which is why we waited on that and got some more height on towards the end of the game.

"I think the credit for tonight has to go solely to the players on the pitch. For everyone that started the game, everyone that came on and everyone that's been involved around it, I thought it was a real well-connected team effort tonight."

On the dismissal of Mumba, who received his marching orders for the second time this term, he added: "I look at the last few games, Bali saved us two or three times in the last few games from those types of recovery runs.

"Tonight, we just got one wrong in terms of our timing and when he tried to win the ball.

"These things happen in football. It's not something we're happy about, but it's not something that I'm going to start criticising. It's just something for us to work on and get better at."

One significant downer on the night arrived with the news that midfielder Archie Collins come off in the second half with a hamstring injury.

McCann commented: "He doesn't look too good. He doesn't look too good.

"He's felt his hamstring, so we'll have to get that scanned tomorrow. So we're a little bit concerned about that one."
