#1784. Real Madrid vs Alaves - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 14:44, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:20

Real Madrid will be aiming to make it 11 straight wins in all competitions when they welcome Alaves to Bernabeu on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last nine games against Alaves, including a 2-1 victory in the corresponding match during the 2025-26 campaign.

Real Madrid will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League, with that success making it 10 victories in a row in all competitions.

Jose Mourinho's side are flying, with their winning run including six in Spain's top flight, and they are currently second in the La Liga table, only three points off the leaders Barcelona.

Los Blancos now have three straight league matches against Alaves, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao before resuming their Champions League campaign away to Arsenal on December 9.

Real Madrid would go level on points with Barcelona should they manage to win this match, and they have been victorious in 38 of their previous 46 games against Alaves in all competitions, suffering only five defeats in the process.

Vinicius Junior is still finding it difficult to show his best form for Real Madrid, but Kylian Mbappe is having another incredible campaign, netting 19 times in 18 appearances in all competitions.

Alaves will be the huge underdogs this weekend, but two of their last three wins over Real Madrid have come away from home, including a 2-1 success at Bernabeu in November 2020.

The Blue and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Deportivo La Coruna, with the result leaving them in ninth spot in the La Liga table on 16 points, boasting a record of four wins, four draws and five defeats from their 13 matches.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have been excellent at home this season, picking up 13 points from seven matches, but they are still waiting for their first away success of the campaign.

Alaves finished 14th in Spain's top flight last season, only one point above the relegation zone, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27.

The Basque outfit will be the fresher of the two teams following Real Madrid's Champions League involvement, but they will be up against a side that have the second-best defensive record (11 conceded) and second-best attacking record (33 scored) during the current season.

Real Madrid will be missing Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg), Ferland Mendy (hip) and Endrick (groin) through injury on Saturday, but no fresh issues have been reported.

There will be changes to the side that took to the field for the first whistle against PSV, with Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen potentially all being introduced into the defence.

Jude Bellingham should also return to the starting side, with Yan Diomande potentially being rested from the first whistle to allow Arda Guler and Vinicius Junior to feature in the wide areas.

As for Alaves, Facundo Garces (knee), Mikel Rodriguez (knee) and Hugo Noava (muscle) are unavailable.

Given the nature of the result and indeed the performance against Deportivo last time out, it is possible that it could be same again in terms of the starting team for the visitors.

Lucas Boye has scored six times in 12 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set to feature in the final third, while Denis Suarez and Antonio Blanco are also set to be in the XI.

Alaves deserve credit for what has been a solid season to date, but Real Madrid are in a good place at the moment, and we are fully expecting Mourinho's side to claim another three points.

#1778. Stockport County vs Leyton Orient - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 15:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:05

Looking to remain top of the League One table heading into the final month of the year, Stockport County welcome Leyton Orient to Edgeley Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Hatters currently hold a three-point lead at the summit after recording their third consecutive victory with a 3-0 win away to Cambridge United, while the O's are hoping to close the gap on the playoff places after beating AFC Wimbledon 4-1 last time out.

Following their agonisingly narrow failure to secure promotion to the Championship last season, Stockport County parted ways with long-serving manager Dave Challinor and appointed former Rochdale boss Jimmy McNulty as his replacement.

McNulty has so far overseen 21 matches in charge of the Hatters across all competitions, recording 13 wins, four draws and four defeats to give him an impressive win rate of 61.9%.

Ten of those victories have come in League One, with Stockport looking to enter December at the top of the table after collecting 32 points from their opening 16 matches, a lead they could extend to six points if results elsewhere go their way and they secure a fourth consecutive league win.

Their impressive league form has also carried over into the cup competitions, with McNulty's men finishing top of their EFL Trophy group and booking their place in the next round of the FA Cup, although they survived a major scare earlier this month, coming from two goals behind to beat Isthmian League side Cray Wanderers 3-2.

More recently, the Greater Manchester outfit climbed to the summit of League One with an emphatic 3-0 victory over Cambridge, a match that featured a superb free-kick from captain Oliver Norwood.

The three goals scored last weekend took Stockport's league tally to 32 for the season, a total bettered by no other side in the third tier and only three teams across England's top four divisions.

As for visitors Leyton Orient, they have enjoyed a more consistent campaign this time around after spending much of the 2025-26 season battling near the bottom of the table and ultimately finishing just one place above the relegation zone.

After their opening 14 League One matches, the London-based side sit 12th under the continued leadership of Richie Wellens, who recently surpassed 250 games in charge of the O's, with six wins, two draws and six defeats leaving them on 20 points.

Although victory on Saturday, at a ground where Stockport boast the best home record in the division, would not be enough to lift Orient into the playoff places, it could leave them just three points outside the top six, with games in hand over all but one of the teams currently above them.

The O's most recently continued their impressive home form with a convincing 4-1 victory over London neighbours AFC Wimbledon, securing their fourth league win in their last five matches at Brisbane Road.

In fact, Wellens' side are already closing in on surpassing their total number of home victories from the whole of last season, having won half of their league fixtures on home soil so far in 2026-27.

Although the two sides finished at opposite ends of the table last season, neither could claim bragging rights in their meetings, with both encounters ending in draws.

The last time either side won this fixture within 90 minutes was in February 2025, the same season they faced each other in the League One playoff semi-finals.

Stockport County form (all competitions):

Leyton Orient also look set to travel from the capital with the option of naming an unchanged starting XI following last weekend's victory.

Former Tottenham Hotspur forward Dane Scarlett is expected to lead the line again after scoring in consecutive matches, while Alex Gilbert should retain his place in midfield after scoring and providing an assist against Wimbledon.

Wellens will, however, remain without Ollie O'Neill, who is expected to miss four months after undergoing surgery shortly after returning from a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare are also expected to remain in the treatment room.

Stockport County possible starting lineup:

Whatmuff; Gordon, O'Connell, Pye; Glover, Bate, Norwood, Ennis; Diamond, Wootton, Wood

Baxter; Stevens, Gilchrist, Edmonds-Green, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, C. Wellens, Dobra; Scarlett

Although Leyton Orient have produced some encouraging results in recent weeks, we expect the league leaders to show why they sit at the top of the table and maintain their push for promotion.

We see Stockport having enough quality to extend their impressive home record and make it four consecutive league victories.

#1776. Police arrest seven men after Man United's 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool at Anfield - with two suspected of illegal tragedy chanting

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, new guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end)

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce issues between the two sets of fans.

#1774. Chelsea news: Xabi Alonso slams Wesley Fofana for interview comments

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:13

Xabi Alonso has revealed that Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for comments made in an interview earlier this week.

The Blues are currently preparing for a Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Sitting in eighth place in the Premier League table after three defeats in four matches, Alonso could have done without any controversy away from the pitch.

Instead, Fofana gave an interview where he revealed that he considered retirement during a prolonged spell on the sidelines with serious knee injuries.

Not only did the Frenchman add that he was convinced to continue playing by his agent because of the money he could earn, Fofana hinted that he was not overly disappointed to miss a spot kick in a penalty shootout against Liverpool last month.

Addressing the situation at a press conference, Alonso suggested that he had been left furious by Fofana's words.

He told reporters: "Absolutely, we have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate.

"He apologised, he knows it was not right the moment, it was not right the content, we are here to take things seriously and he said that it's not going to be repeated and we know that it's something that we don't want, these kind of things and they are not going to be repeated for sure."

The Spaniard added that he now regarded the matter as "closed", indicating that Fofana remains available to face Forest.

Fofana's place in the Chelsea defence had already been in doubt due to the level of his performance in the 4-1 defeat versus Leeds last weekend.

Although there have been games this season where the 25-year-old has played to an acceptable standard, his attitude and decision-making in the Chelsea backline has been questioned for months.

Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury has led to Fofana partnering Levi Colwill, but they have performed poorly both individually and as a partnership.

#1772. Camarda recalls emotion of disallowed UCL goal and Gabbia’s words: “I burst into tears”

Francesco Camarda has spoken about his Champions League goal that never was today, and how it was an AC Milan dream come true.

Camarda first became known to Milan as a youngster, but he announced himself further when he became Serie A’s youngest-ever appearance maker. He almost then went to a European level, with a goal in the Champions League. However, it wasn’t to be.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

On his debut in the competition, the starlet bagged a goal which would’ve made him the Rossoneri’s youngest-ever scorer in Europe’s main stage. Yet it was ruled out for offside and a few years on, the now 18-year-old is still waiting for a first competitive goal for the Diavolo.

Speaking to Vice, the striker opened up about his dream of playing in the Champions League at San Siro, his emotions after his goal (and it later being disallowed) and how his teammates rallied around him, as MilanVibes relayed.

“As a child, I used to say to my dad: imagine if one day I could walk into San Siro and hear the Champions League anthem, accompanied by the roar of the entire stadium. When it actually happened, I thought back to that little boy and realised I had realised a dream.

“When I stepped onto the pitch, I had an incredible adrenaline rush. Then the goal came, and I felt the whole stadium explode. I also felt the affection of my teammates, who immediately raised me into the air.

“However, when I looked at the scoreboard and saw that the VAR check was in progress, I was already convinced the goal would be disallowed.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”

“I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”

“In football, there are positive and negative opinions; it has always been this way and will continue to be this way. A player’s true strength lies in not being influenced by what is said, because, regardless of whether you do well or badly, someone will always find a reason to judge you.”

#1771. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

Mason Mount is fit enough for the bench and takes Shea Lacey’s seat

Brennan Johnson comes in for Iliman Ndiaye, now at Man City. Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jack Grealish start on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @ManUtd. COYB! 🔵#EVEMUN pic.twitter.com/8s2UrcwR59

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1770. Leicester City vs Mansfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 15:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:01

Leicester City will be looking to continue their unbeaten run when they welcome Mansfield Town to the King Power Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit seventh in the League One table, while the visitors are 14th.

Leicester City are unbeaten in their last four league games and they picked up a hugely important 1-0 victory over Huddersfield Town last weekend.

Louis Page scored the only goal of the game as Huddersfield suffered just their second league defeat, but Leicester were unable to carry that momentum into a clash with managerless Blackpool on Tuesday.

The Foxes were held to a 1-1 draw by Blackpool, with Will Alves giving Russell Martin's side the lead in the 66th minute before Niall Ennis bagged a late equaliser.

Martin described the draw as the most frustrating result of his managerial career and he will be expecting an immediate response on Saturday.

Mansfield, meanwhile, are without a win in their last three league games and were held to a 1-1 draw by MK Dons last weekend.

Callum Paterson headed home a late equaliser for MK Dons after Michael Smith gave Mansfield the lead in the first half.

Nigel Clough's side have also drawn 0-0 with Wigan Athletic and lost 2-0 to Notts County in recent league action, leaving them 14th in the division with 20 points from 14 matches.

Injury problems have had a major effect on Mansfield's form, with Clough adamant that a fully-fit squad is "good enough to compete in the top half", but they have had some much-needed boosts in recent weeks.

Leicester remain without Will Smallbone after he picked up an injury against Huddersfield.

Emil Riis is set to continue up front for the Foxes, while Page is expected to start alongside John Lundstram in midfield.

Lucas Akins and Liam Thompson will remain sidelined until the end of December, while David McGoldrick's recovery from a knee injury is "week-to-week".

John Terry believes that Arsenal star David Raya is ‘100 per cent’ the best goalkeeper in world football at present.

Raya joined Arsenal on an initial loan deal from Brentford in August 2023 before his move was made permanent for £27 million the following year.

The 31-year-old was an integral part in Arsenal’s success last season, in which the team won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final, where they were beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain.

Raya has continued that form this season to help Arsenal open up a six-point lead at the top of the table after 11 games, and Terry believes the Spaniard is without doubt the world’s best shotstopper.

‘You look at Raya, who they brought in, who knew he was that good?’ Terry said in an interview with Rory Jennings.

#1767. Montella describes ‘dream’ Milan opportunity, Berlusconi and the Supercoppa: “An incredible feeling”

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

This is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”

“He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

“I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”

“It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

“We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”

“I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

“And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen new players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

“Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”

#1766. Wrexham vs Portsmouth - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:25

Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.

Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.

After overseeing just three wins in the first 13 league games, Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has eased some of the pressure that was building on his shoulders with a four-game unbeaten run.

Wrexham went into the international window on the back of a 2-0 win over Middlesbrough and a 1-1 draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, before they returned to action with a narrow 1-0 victory over Lincoln City at Sincil Bank.

They then took the lead in Tuesday’s away clash with Bristol City, but were ultimately forced to settle for a point after Joe Worrall saw his opener cancelled out by Cam Pring’s equaliser, leaving Wrexham in 14th spot in the Championship table and five points adrift of the top eight.

After playing back-to-back away games, Wrexham will be looking forward to returning to the familiar surroundings of the Racecourse Ground, where they have taken seven points from their last three outings since losing to West Bromwich Albion last month.

Wrexham are also one of six teams to score in every Championship home match this term, extending their overall run to at least one goal in each of their last 15 home league games since drawing a blank in a 2-0 loss to Millwall over seven months ago.

In fact, that scoring run includes a 2-1 victory in their recent meeting with Portsmouth in February, which came courtesy of first-half goals from Sam Smith and Max Cleworth.

Portsmouth, meanwhile, are just one point adrift of the playoffs after winning five, drawing three and losing just one of their last nine matches.

After losing to Stoke City before the international window, Pompey resumed their campaign with a hard-fought away draw against Bolton Wanderers before they claimed a 1-0 win in their first home meeting with West Ham United in 14 years.

Odin Bailey’s maiden Portsmouth goal proved enough to secure the club’s first head-to-head victory since a 1-0 success at Upton Park in April 2008, while also keeping their first home clean sheet since the start of September.

John Mousinho’s side will now head on their travels with hopes of extending their four-game unbeaten away run, which started with a 1-0 win over Norwich City and continued with three consecutive draws on the road.

No Championship team has conceded fewer away goals than Portsmouth, whose defence has been breached just six times in their eight road trips this season.

Given the fact they only took a point from their two meetings with Wrexham last term, Pompey will head into Saturday's fixture with hopes of claiming their first head-to-head league win since recording a 2-0 away victory in January 1983.

Wrexham forward Sam Smith will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury earlier this month.

The hosts are also likely to be without the services of Liberato Cacace, Seb Revan, Josh Windass, Callum O’Hare and Nathan Broadhead.

Ollie Rathbone and Kieffer Moore - the latter of whom is Wrexham’s top scorer with five Championship goals to his name this term - are pushing for starting berths.

Jayden Meghoma will be out for up to 10 weeks after sustaining an ankle ligament injury in last weekend’s draw against Bolton.

Meghoma is the latest addition to a lengthy injury list that features Keshi Anderson, Luke Brooke-Smith, Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Connor Ogilvie and Benjamin Arthur.

Marlon Pack, Josh Murphy and Adrian Segecic are options to start if Mousinho decides to freshen up his side for Saturday’s away trip.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Dobson, Whiteman, Ekomie; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Pack, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Murphy; Shade

Portsmouth have conceded more than one goal in just one of their eight away league games this term, and with that in mind, we think they will do enough to avoid defeat in Saturday's fixture.

However, we believe they will fall short of claiming maximum points against a Wrexham side that are unbeaten in four games.

#1765. Elche vs Atletico Madrid - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 15:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:27

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Elche on Saturday evening.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their last four games against Elche, with Los Franjiverdes enjoying the better of their recent meetings.

Elche have been victorious in two of their last four matches against Atletico, with those successes coming at home, including a 3-2 win in their last meeting in April of this year.

Los Franjiverdes will be the fresher of the two teams entering this match, with Atletico in Champions League action on Wednesday, but the hosts have only managed to pick up one point from the last nine available in Spain's top flight.

Martin Anselmi's side played out a 1-1 draw with Levante last time out, with that result following back-to-back defeats to Valencia and Real Betis.

Elche boast a record of two wins, five draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 11 points leaving them in 19th spot in the La Liga table.

Anselmi's team have the worst home record in Spain's top flight this season, having only managed to pick up one point from their six games in front of their own supporters.

Atletico, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 win over Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Alexander Sorloth and Julian Alvarez on the scoresheet.

Simeone's side have a record of 10 wins, one draw and two defeats from their 13 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with 31 points leaving them in third spot in the table.

Atletico are only two points off second-placed Real Madrid and five from the leaders Barcelona, so they are firmly in a title race heading towards the start of December.

The Red and Whites recorded a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight last time out, with Simeone's team responding impressively to their 2-1 reverse to Barcelona before the November international break.

Atletico now have three straight league matches against Elche, Barcelona and Real Betis before returning to European action away to PSV Eindhoven on December 9.

Elche are again expected to be without the services of Ruben Sanchez, Adam Boayar, Ali Houary, Marc Aguado and Yago Santiago due to injury problems.

Fer Nino has been in strong form for the hosts this season, scoring six goals in 13 appearances, and the 26-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also expected to be a spot in the attack for Abiel Osorio, who has one goal and one assist in 11 appearances for Elche during the current campaign.

As for Atletico, Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero will again miss out due to injury problems, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape, with no fresh issues being reported following their Champions League clash with Viking.

Head coach Simeone is expected to introduce Pablo Barrios and Giuliano Simeone back into his starting side, with Sorloth and Lee Kang-in potentially dropping out.

Alvarez has only scored three times during a difficult season to date, with just one of those coming in Spain's top flight, but the Argentine should continue in the final third of the field.

Dituro; Sangare, Redondo Solari, Chust, Revivo; Cepeda, Morcillo, Villar, Valera; Osorio, Nino

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Koke, Simeone, Barrios, Cardoso, Baena; Alvarez

Elche's recent record against Atletico will hand them confidence ahead of this match, but we are expecting Simeone's side to navigate their way to an important three points.

#1764. Manchester United handed huge transfer boost as left-back ‘wants £50m move’

Manchester United have been handed a boost in their transfer pursuit of Maxi Araujo.

That is according to Sport Witness, who claim that the Red Devils could seal a deal worth between €50million and €60m for the left-back.

The left-sided full-back position has been a source of real problems for United, and particularly for new manager Mauricio Pochettino, who is still awaiting his first win in charge since his arrival last week.

The Argentine took the reins at Old Trafford last Wednesday, leading his side to Anfield for a 4-0 debut demolition before a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In that Sporting side was Araujo, 26, who is believed to be open to a move to the Premier League.

The Uruguay international has previously been linked with a switch to the north west amid the pending expiry of Luke Shaw’s contract and Harry Amass’ uncertain future at Old Trafford.

Now, Sport Witness claim that United’s scouts took advantage of their fixture in the Portuguese capital to make a proper assessment of Araujo, with there thought to be appreciation of the player.

The Uruguayan is understood to have a €80m release clause in his contract at the Primeira Liga outfit, but it is believed that United would be able to negotiate the asking price down.

In Shaw’s injury-hit absence this term, Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was forced to field natural right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on the left side of defence, while Pochettino has favoured centre-half Lisandro Martinez in that position since he came in.

#1763. Chelsea injury news: One fit, two out as Xabi Alonso provides update ahead of Nottingham Forest game

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:41

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Moises Caicedo is available for Friday's Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest.

The Ecuador international has found himself in and out of the Blues starting lineup this season due to several fitness issues.

Caicedo's latest injury came during the first half of last weekend's game versus Leeds United, the midfielder landing awkwardly on his back and needing to be withdrawn.

As a result, Caicedo has been an obvious injury doubt for what is a potentially-crucial game for Alonso after three defeats in four top-flight games.

However, speaking at his pre-match press conference, the Spaniard declared Caicedo available for selection.

He told reporters: "Yes, he's going to be OK for tomorrow."

On a negative note, Alonso acknowledged that Joao Pedro would remain sidelined for the trip to the East Midlands.

Meanwhile, providing an update on Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury, he added: "It's one less week than the last game so we are closer to recovery but not for this game."

There have been reports which suggest that Lacroix could return earlier than the initial target return period of January.

With Lacroix still injured, Alonso may feel forced to start Wesley Fofana alongside Levi Colwill, despite being furious with the Frenchman's comments in an interview this week.

There is the possibility of Josh Acheampong starting in the centre with Colwill, with Marco Palestra potentially starting at right-back.

If Jorrel Hato remains sidelined with a back injury, Pep Chavarria is favourite to start at left-back.

Alonso also has the option of going with a back three featuring the aforementioned centre-backs, with Pedro Neto at right wing-back and Palestra on the left.

#1762. How Amorim picked apart Alvini’s gung-ho approach: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

Gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

From there, though, the Rossoneri ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both scored within minutes of coming off the bench, finishing counter-attacks, then Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper. Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive. However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up. Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

— Rohit Rajeev (@keralista) November 23, 2026

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

This movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

Frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

The second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

Frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine quickly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

After the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

Pulisic, meanwhile, used the bridge of his foot to execute a delicate chip, lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper and completing the counter-attack.

⚽️ GOAL CHRISTIAN PULISIC 🇺🇸 https://t.co/B4mP55RJ8u

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

We wrote something during the break about how Milan are over-performing relative to certain metrics. Above all, their actual goals scored was/is well above their Expected Goals, helped by the fact four players are converting an abnormally high percentage of chances.

With this in mind, the stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals, so they again out-performed what they created. And yet, the Rossoneri racked up five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

So, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. Many would argue that Milan could have scored more given their brilliant on Sunday, yet xG would have you believe it was a ‘lucky’ margin in a game that should have been 2/3-1.

The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season, but thankfully Amorim’s side managed to deal with them all relatively well.
